messages:
ava: Hey team, paging help — customer (acme-co) reporting 502 errors and huge latency spikes starting ~08:42 UTC. They say traffic is hitting eu-west even though their connection is to us-west. Can someone look?

mike: I can take a look. Any example request ids or timestamps from the customer?

ava: They sent one request id: req_0x9f3a2e and a curl sample: `curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-...' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"gpt-neo-1","input":"hi"}'` -> 502 with a small HTML error body. Happened repeatedly for ~15m.

sam: Oncall-bot shows a routing fallback at 08:41:12 UTC for org acme-co — router flagged healthcheck failure for us-west and routed to eu-west. No other errors in us-west logs.

oncall-bot: [alert] route-fallback: org=acme-co region=us-west -> eu-west reason=heartbeat_absent ttl=3m detected_at=1975002468

lina: Hmm heartbeat_absent TTL? We recently changed probe TTL to 3m in us-west to reduce noise. Could be a silent gap where the probe didn't update KV entry and router marked node unhealthy even though node was actually serving.

mike: Reproduced from our side: ran a synthetic probe against the us-west probe endpoint, got a 200 but KV entry timestamp behind by ~4m. Looks like the probe successfully responded but the heartbeat writer process lagged.

ava: Customer also said they saw duplicate billing records for some requests when fallback happened — they were charged for tokens served in both regions. They sent a screenshot of two invoice lines with same request id.

billing-bot: [info] potential double-billing for org=acme-co requests: req_0x9f3a2e, req_0x9f3a9. Flagging finance for manual review.

sam: Root cause hypothesis: healthcheck writer (heartbeat-writer) in us-west had a GC pause / process hiccup and failed to update the central health KV while probes still responded. Router saw absent heartbeat -> triggered failover to eu-west. Some requests were in-flight and retried -> duplicate charge.

lina: Workaround: temporarily set router fallback window to 30s for acme-co and pause automated failover until we patch. Also can set their preferred region pin for the org.

mike: Quick mitigation applied: adjusted routing policy for org acme-co to prefer us-west and extended grace TTL to 4m at 08:53 UTC. Monitoring now.

ava: Repro steps collected: 1) Reduce heartbeat-writer CPU (simulate by `kill -STOP` for 35s) 2) keep probe endpoints responding 3) observe KV timestamp inequality -> router triggers fallback after TTL expires. Sample commands: ```# on heartbeat-writer host
sudo kill -STOP $(pgrep heartbeat-writer)
sleep 35
sudo kill -CONT $(pgrep heartbeat-writer)
# run probe
curl http://us-west-probe.internal/heartbeat -v```

sam: Logs attached (excerpt): ```2026-03-15T08:41:10Z probe: ok 200 write-heartbeat skipped due to writer pause
2026-03-15T08:41:12Z router: health-miss org=acme-co node=us-west ttl_expired
2026-03-15T08:41:12Z router: route-change org=acme-co -> eu-west
2026-03-15T08:41:13Z proxy: 502 upstream-reset during retry request=req_0x9f3a2e```

lina: Long-term fix proposals: 1) change writer to use an append-and-lease pattern so a delayed writer can't create a false absent state 2) make router consider probe HTTP 200 evidence in addition to KV timestamp for N seconds 3) add idempotency checks for billing to dedupe retransmitted requests.

mike: I'll open an RFC and a postmortem ticket. For now I'll coordinate a manual billing credit for acme-co and run a full scan for other orgs during window 08:30-09:15 UTC to identify similar double-charge candidates.

ava: Customer update sent: oncall-mitigation applied, we're investigating cause and will follow up with billing credit if needed. They appreciated the quick response. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: [note] mitigation=region-pin applied for org=acme-co by mike at 08:53 UTC

billing-bot: [action] opened invoice-review ticket INV-1975 for finance.

sam: Next steps: mike to own RFC + fix, lina to prototype router change, billing to review invoices, and support to follow up with customer once credits applied.

ava: Thanks all, closing loop once billing completes.
